column2: Basic web development with LLM support
column3:
• Use Copilot to help build a multi-file web app.
• Set up VS Code with Live Preview.
• Learn HTML5 structure, start tags, content, end tags, headings, paragraphs, bold, italic, horizontal rules, nested elements, divs and spans.
• Link CSS in three ways: inline, internal, and external.
• Use element, ID, and class selectors.
• Write CSS rules with a selector, property, value, and line ending.
column4:
• VS Code with Live Preview
• W3Schools HTML + CSS tutorials
• Copilot Web
column5:
• Activity:
  • create a working two-page HTML and CSS cafe site with linked pages and at least three selector types.

• Takeaway:
  • push the cafe website activity to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Include Home and Menu pages, images, navigation, headings, sections, and external CSS.
column7: Research and apply emerging web technology trends

column3:
• Learn JavaScript basics: variables, if/else, for loops, functions, events, load order, JavaScript libraries, Bootstrap, and AI context.
• Add simple interaction to a web page and break repeated code into functions.
column4:
• VS Code with Live Preview
• W3Schools JavaScript tutorials
• Copilot Web
column5:
• Activity:
  • demonstrate one working JavaScript interaction and explain the event, function, and variables used.

• Takeaway:
  • push the improved cafe site to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Add one Bootstrap component and one custom JavaScript feature.
column7: Customise complex ICT content management systems

column3:
• Explore how AI can be used as more than a chatbot.
• Use AI tools and agents to plan and complete small coding tasks.
• Practise writing clear prompts and keeping token use low.
column5:
• Activity:
  • complete or plan a small agent-assisted coding task and save the prompts used.

• Takeaway:
  • push the activity to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Add a short reflection on how agents can help web development and one risk to watch for.

column3: • Use this week to catch up, troubleshoot, and extend skills from HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and AI tools.
column5:
• Activity:
  • complete an individual progress check for Weeks 1 to 3 skills.

• Takeaway:
  • push the cleaned-up portfolio folder to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.

column3:
• Learn how data moves from Data to API to Front End.
• Connect MockAPI or DummyJSON to a front end.
• Build a login page using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and fetch.
column5:
• Activity:
  • create a front end that fetches and displays data from DummyJSON or MockAPI.

• Takeaway:
  • push the API display activity to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Show at least five records in cards, a list, or a table.

column3:
• Learn the idea of server-side rendering, frameworks, and how to improve a login page.
• Improve layout, validation messages, labels, and visual design.
column5:
• Activity:
  • improve the login page with validation and accessible labels.

• Takeaway:
  • push the redesigned login page to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Include a short before and after note.

column3:
• Start a Next.js project.
• Learn the app structure, TypeScript basics, reusable components, static routes, dynamic routes, and shared layouts.
column5:
• Activity:
  • create a Next.js app with two static routes, one dynamic route, and a shared layout.

• Takeaway:
  • push the mini portfolio or product catalogue to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.

column3:
• Use events, arrow functions, and React state.
• Build small interactive components such as counters, toggles, filters, favourites, or simple forms.
column5:
• Activity:
  • build a component where the screen changes when the user interacts with it.

• Takeaway:
  • push the updated Next.js project to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Add two interactive features and comments explaining the state and events.

column3:
• Complete a timed practice task that combines components, routing, styling, state, and basic data handling.
• Practise reading requirements, planning work, and testing.
column5:
• Activity:
  • submit the practice assessment attempt and complete a self-check against the marking criteria.

• Takeaway:
  • push the practice task to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Revise weak areas and bring questions for assessment week.

column3: • Complete the formal assessment task using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, AI-supported development, and Next.js skills.
column5:
• Assessment:
  • complete and submit the required assessment evidence.

• Takeaway:
  • push final evidence to GitHub where required and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Add screenshots, notes, or reflection if required.

column3:
• Revise Next.js and arrow functions.
• Review project structure, routing, components, and common errors.
• Refactor one component to make it clearer.
column5:
• Activity:
  • correct or refactor one component that uses arrow functions clearly.

• Takeaway:
  • push the revised component to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Document three improvements you made.

column3:
• Use fetch from a button with useState.
• Learn async code, JSON, APIs, loading states, and showing useful fields on the page.
column5:
• Activity:
  • build a button that fetches API data and updates the page using useState.

• Takeaway:
  • push the fetch activity to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Connect to a different endpoint and display the data clearly.

column3:
• Continue using fetch, useState, async code, and JSON.
• Add error handling, empty states, loading messages, and clearer data formatting.
column5:
• Activity:
  • update the fetch component so it handles success, loading, and error states.

• Takeaway:
  • push the updated API feature to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Include evidence of loading, success, and error states where possible.

column3:
• Use useEffect for work that should happen when a page loads.
• Compare button-based fetch with automatic fetch.
• Learn dependency arrays and how to avoid repeated fetch loops.
column5:
• Activity:
  • load API data automatically using useEffect without repeated fetch loops.

• Takeaway:
  • push the useEffect version to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Explain when button fetch and page-load fetch are useful.

column3:
• Start using the Shadcn component library.
• Add a button, card, or form component.
• Learn how component libraries speed up UI work but still need good design choices.
column5:
• Activity:
  • add and customise at least one Shadcn component in the app.

• Takeaway:
  • push the Shadcn activity to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Replace one plain UI section with Shadcn components.

column3:
• Continue using Shadcn.
• Build a more complete interface with components such as cards, dialogs, forms, tables, navigation, or alerts.
• Focus on consistency and accessibility.
column5:
• Activity:
  • build a mini interface that uses several Shadcn components consistently.

• Takeaway:
  • push the polished UI to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Prepare a short demo explaining your component choices.

column3:
• Learn how Supabase can work as a content management system.
• Discuss projects, tables, records, and how a front end can read managed content.
column5:
• Activity:
  • draft a content model and, if available, display Supabase data in the app.

• Takeaway:
  • push the Supabase planning or connection activity to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Include fields and sample records.

column3:
• Continue using Supabase as a content management system.
• Improve how data is displayed.
• Plan or build simple create and update workflows.
• Discuss permissions, keys, and safe setup.
column5:
• Activity:
  • show CMS-style content in the app and outline or mock a create/update workflow.

• Takeaway:
  • push the updated Supabase work to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Add notes on how the front end uses the Supabase data.

column3:
• Prepare a project for deployment.
• Check build errors, set environment variables if needed, deploy to Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, or an FTP server, and test the live site.
column5:
• Activity:
  • deploy the project or document the deployment attempt and any errors.

• Takeaway:
  • push the deployed project files to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Include the live link and a short release note.

column3: • Complete a second practice task focused on building features, using data, polishing the UI, and preparing for deployment.
column5:
• Activity:
  • submit the practice assessment attempt with a completed checklist.

• Takeaway:
  • push the practice task to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Revise based on feedback and prepare final evidence.

column3: • Complete the formal assessment task using interface development, API/data, components, CMS, and deployment skills.
column5:
• Assessment:
  • complete and submit the required assessment evidence.

• Takeaway:
  • push final evidence to GitHub where required and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Include deployment links, documentation, or reflection notes if required.

column3:
• Plan the project scope.
• Define user needs, pages, components, data, and required features.
• Create a simple backlog or checklist.
column5:
• Activity:
  • complete a project proposal, feature list, and first wireframe or backlog.

• Takeaway:
  • push the project plan to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Prepare assets, content, data sources, or API needs for next week.

column3:
• Build and polish the project.
• Complete core features, test user flows, improve UI consistency, fix issues, and prepare the final demo.
column5:
• Activity:
  • present a project demo or progress review showing the core features working.

• Takeaway:
  • push the final project to GitHub and submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site.
  • Include deployment link, screenshots, and reflection.

• Submission workflow:
  • students push each activity to GitHub, then submit the GitHub link through the Checkpoint site so trainers can review completion.
